elements.char: UTLOOK
elements.label: text

elements.char: All our experiments were carried out on 2D images. With
elements.label: text

elements.char: minor mathematical modifications, the proposed method can
elements.label: text

elements.char: be applied to learn sampling patterns for 3D MRI, though
elements.label: text

elements.char: it is worth noting that the computational effort will scale up
elements.label: text

elements.char: accordingly and the implementation will need to be optimised
elements.label: text

elements.char: to deal with this. There is considerable scope for optimisation
elements.label: text

elements.char: of the computational implementation of the method, for in-
elements.label: text

elements.char: stance by parallelising the solution method for the lower level
elements.label: text

elements.char: problems. To accelerate MRI in practice, it is necessary to take
elements.label: text

elements.char: into account the physical constraints imposed on sampling.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The free pattern of points learned by our method is not
elements.label: text

elements.char: immediately useful for accelerating 2D MRI, but it can be
elements.label: text

elements.char: used for accelerated 3D MRI. If our method is extended to 3D
elements.label: text

elements.char: MRI, the problem of efficiently sampling along these patterns
elements.label: text

elements.char: in practice comes up again. In [43], a method is proposed
elements.label: text

elements.char: (which has been implemented in practice at NeuroSpin [44])
elements.label: text

elements.char: that can be used to generate practical sampling strategies from
elements.label: text

elements.char: a given target density. We can estimate a target density from
elements.label: text

elements.char: our learned pattern, and use it as an input to this method.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Besides these extensions to our method, one can consider
elements.label: text

elements.char: more general lower level regularisation functionals and allow
elements.label: text

elements.char: for more flexibility to learn a custom regulariser as was done
elements.label: text

elements.char: for denoising in [45], or unroll the lower level algorithm and
elements.label: text

elements.char: use an approach similar to that of the variational network [46].
elements.label: text

elements.char: In this work, we have considered the free and Cartesian line
elements.label: text

elements.char: parametrisations of the sampling pattern, but we mentioned
elements.label: text

elements.char: that any differentiable parametrisation of the sampling pattern
elements.label: text

elements.char: can be used. With an appropriate choice of the parametrisation,
elements.label: text

elements.char: our method can be used to learn optimal radial line patterns,
elements.label: text

elements.char: or other physically feasible optimal sampling patterns.
elements.label: text

elements.char: In our framework, we made smoothness assumptions on the
elements.label: text

elements.char: lower level problems in order to differentiate their solution
elements.label: text

elements.char: maps. Similar results can be derived assuming partial smooth-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ness of the regularisation functionals [47], which covers total
elements.label: text

elements.char: variation regularisation and the wavelet regularisation without
elements.label: text

elements.char: needing to smooth them. The non-smooth lower level problems
elements.label: text

elements.char: will be harder to solve, but it might be possible to deal directly
elements.label: text

elements.char: with non-smooth lower level problems using this approach.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Alternatively, one could consider optimality conditions for
elements.label: text

elements.char: bilevel optimisation problems with non-smooth lower level
elements.label: text

elements.char: problems [48] and attempt to solve the optimality conditions.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Despite being a smooth optimisation problem, the learning
elements.label: text

elements.char: procedure is computationally intensive, since the lower level
elements.label: text

elements.char: problems have to be solved to high accuracy in each iteration.
elements.label: text

elements.char: These issues are alleviated by warm-starting the lower level
elements.label: text

elements.char: solvers and it may be possible to do something similar with
elements.label: text

elements.char: the iterative solver used to compute gradients. There is consid-
elements.label: text

elements.char: erable scope for investigating ways in which the optimisation
elements.label: text

elements.char: can be improved: the problem is non-convex so one could
elements.label: text

elements.char: further research whether this is problematic in this case, and,
elements.label: text

elements.char: if so, how to get around these issues. In Section III-C, we saw
elements.label: text

elements.char: that, even with the penalty in the upper level that encourages
elements.label: text

elements.char: discreteness of the learned patterns, the learned Cartesian line
elements.label: text

elements.char: patterns were not binary, which may be an artefact of the diffi-
elements.label: text

elements.char: culties involved in solving the optimisation problem. One thing
elements.label: text

elements.char: that can be of great importance in non-convex optimisation is
elements.label: text

elements.char: the initialisation that is used; in this work we have used a
elements.label: text

elements.char: fixed initialisation consisting of an identity sampling operator
elements.label: text

elements.char: and the corresponding optimal regularisation parameter and
elements.label: text

elements.char: found that it generally worked well, but more detailed study
elements.label: text

elements.char: may point to a more suitable initialisation. Since the objective
elements.label: text

elements.char: function splits as a sum over the training set, another natural
elements.label: text

elements.char: direction of future research would be to investigate the use of
elements.label: text

elements.char: stochastic optimisation methods in this setting.

elements.char: ONCLUSIONS
elements.label: text

elements.char: We have proposed a supervised learning approach to learn
elements.label: text

elements.char: high quality sampling patterns for accelerated MRI for a given
elements.label: text

elements.char: variational reconstruction method. We have demonstrated that
elements.label: text

elements.char: this approach is highly flexible, allowing for a wide variety of
elements.label: text

elements.char: regularisation functionals to be used and allowing constraints
elements.label: text

elements.char: to be imposed on the learned sampling patterns. Furthermore,
